I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates Regional Governments to regulate and manage their own regions for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional governments is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in their regions.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, protection and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development as well as the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that girls should be protected by the state, particularly against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women and children, especially for the Region. The Region is one of the most authorized parties in carrying out women's empowerment and child protection by implementing and formulating regulations in order to provide guarantees for women's empowerment and child protection.

One form of such regulation is Regional Regulation. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women and children who are victims of violence.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates Regional Governments to regulate and manage their own regions for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates Regional Governments to regulate and manage their own regions for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional governments is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in their regions.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, protection and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development as well as the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that girls should be protected by the state, particularly against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women and children, especially for the Region. The Region is one of the most authorized parties in carrying out women's empowerment and child protection by implementing and formulating regulations in order to provide guarantees for women's empowerment and child protection.

One form of such regulation is Regional Regulation. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women and children who are victims of violence.

6.7.rationale: The Indonesian text explains the nondiscrimination principle (Penjelasan Pasal 2 huruf c) as not differentiating “suku, ras, agama, … asal kebangsaan … atau faktor lainnya.” This is an explicit recognition of minority-related categories (ethnicity/race/religion/national origin). The regulation does not provide targeted measures for minority women, but it does include minority categories within nondiscrimination. If the indicator is about inclusion/recognition of minority groups (not necessarily targeted programs), the golden ‘Yes’ is supported. The judge predicted ‘No’ because the retrieved candidates for 6.7 did not include the Penjelasan Pasal 2 huruf c passage; thus retrieval failed to surface the relevant minority-language evidence.
